newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-JONES OUTDUELS MARTINEZ TO PICK UP 10TH WIN FOR METS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-JONES OUTDUELS MARTINEZ TO PICK UP 10TH WIN FOR METS.

text.p: Bobby Jones outdueled Pedro Martinez to become the first 10-game winner in the National League as the New York Mets edged the Montreal Espos 2-1 on Tuesday.
Carlos Baerga delivered a two-out RBI double in the bottom of the eighth inning to rally the Mets to victory.
Jones (10-2), who has won his last seven starts, allowed a run and four hits with three walks and five strikeouts. His 10 wins in 12 starts set a Mets record.

"Each and every win is important," said Jones, who is tied with Toronto's Roger Clemens for the major-league lead in wins. "Obviously, (Martinez) is one of the top pitchers around. Whenever you beat one of the best, it's a great feeling."
John Franco pitched a scoreless ninth for his 15th save.
Baerga, who was 3-for-4 with a double and a triple, has raised his batting average to .299. He is 7-for-10 against Martinez this season.
"I don't know if I have his number," Baerga said. "I'm just hitting the ball pretty good."
Martinez (8-2) tied his career high with 12 strikeouts. He gave up two runs and seven hits over eight innings.
The pitchers locked up in a classic duel that left the game scoreless after seven innings.
The Expos scored their lone run in the top of the eighth when Rondell White doubled home Mark Grudzielanek. But the Mets answered with two in the bottom of the inning.
In Houston, Jeff Bagwell's solo homer with one out in the bottom of the 10th inning lifted the Houston Astros to a 4-3 win over the Los Angeles Dodgers.

Scott Radinsky (2-1) began the 10th for Los Angeles, which had evened the score with two runs in the top of the eighth. He retired Thomas Howard to begin the inning, but surrendered Bagwell's 18th homer to left-centre on a 3-2 pitch.
Bagwell, who leads the National League in homers, had struck out swinging three times and walked prior to his game-winner.
In St Louis, John Mabry hit a three-run homer and drove in a six runs and Royce Clayton had five hits to lead a 21-hit attack as the Cardinals crushed the Colorado Rockies 15-4.
Mabry, who went 3-for-4, and Ron Gant each hit three-run homers in a seven-run fifth inning.
Matt Morris (3-3) picked up the win, allowing four runs and four hits over six innings. Bobby Jones (1-1) suffered the loss, surrendering six runs and eight hits with one walk.

In Atlanta, John Flaherty's RBI groundout with the bases loaded snapped a 2-2 ninth-inning tie and Quilvio Veras added a two-run single as the San Diego Padres beat the Braves 5-2 for their fifth consecutive victory.

Wally Joyner led off the ninth with a single off closer Mark Wohlers (2-1) and Greg Vaughn walked. Wohlers bobbled Chris Gomez's sacrifice bunt, loading the bases and Flaherty hit a hard grounder to first baseman Fred McGriff as pinch-runner Archi Cianfrocco scored for a 3-2 lead.
Wohlers struck out pinch-hitter Craig Shipley, but Veras singled up the middle, scoring Vaughn and Gomez.

In Chicago, Steve Cooke allowed one run over 7 1/3 innings and Jose Guillen's fourth-inning double drove in the go-ahead run as the Pittsburgh Pirates snapped the Cubs' three-game winning streak with a 3-1 victory.
Cooke (5-6) allowed five hits, walked one and struck out five. His only mistake came in the third inning when Scott Servais led off with a homer for the Cubs.
Steve Trachsel (3-5) suffered the loss, allowing two runs and eight hits in eight innings with seven strikeouts and no walks.
In Philadelphia, Kent Mercker allowed one run and two hits over 6 1/3 innings as the Cincinnati Reds sent the Phillies to their fifth straight loss with a 3-2 victory.
Merker (3-5) walked four and struck out five to win his second straight start against the Phillies. Jeff Shaw survived a shaky ninth to record his eighth save.
Merker retired the last 19 batters he faced without allowing a hit and walked three.
Eddie Taubensee, Willie Greene and Joe Oliver each drove in a run for the Reds.
At Florida, Shawn Estes allowed a run in six innings and homered to lead the San Francisco Giants to a 9-1 victory over the Marlins in a game reduced to six-plus innings due to rain.
Estes (8-2) gave up two hits, walked five, struck out four and stroked his first major-league homer in the fifth inning en route to his fourth straight win.
J.T. Snow homered and Bill Mueller added his first major-league home run for the Giants, who rocked Alex Fernandez (5-6) for seven runs and 10 hits.
